facts.text: Hickory Ridge first got its post office in 1875, when the Brushy Lake Township post office was named after the town.
The town emerged in the 1870s as a small settlement during the post‑Civil War expansion into Arkansas’s rural areas.
After the Cotton Belt railway reached the area in 1882, Hickory Ridge prospered from timber and agriculture, and the post office reopened in 1892.
Hickory Ridge incorporated in 1949, a late move that mirrored post‑World War II trends in rural Arkansas where towns sought municipal status to manage local governance.
The city sits within the Mississippi embayment of the Delta, a flat fertile floodplain that shapes its agricultural landscape.
Row agriculture dominates today, with soybeans and cotton leading, while commercial aquaculture—crawfish, baitfish, and catfish farms—is also common.
